mechanism: MEMPOOL-ADD passes (mempool-entry-vsize entry) as the txgraph size (src/mempool/mempool.lisp:1008-1010, and the package path at :1404), and that slot is SIGOP-ADJUSTED-VSIZE = ceil(max(weight, sigops * 20) / 4) (:130-138, set in make-entry-from-tx at :255-256); +max-cluster-size+ is 101000 vB (src/mempool/txgraph.lisp:49). Core's TxGraph works in WEIGHT throughout: StageAddition builds FeePerWeight(fee, GetSigOpsAdjustedWeight(GetTransactionWeight(tx), sigops_cost, nBytesPerSigOp)) (refs/bitcoin/src/txmempool.cpp:1017 at d3056bc), where GetSigOpsAdjustedWeight is max(weight, sigop_cost * bytes_per_sigop) with NO division (policy/policy.cpp:376-379), and MakeTxGraph is handed max_cluster_size = limits.cluster_size_vbytes * WITNESS_SCALE_FACTOR = 404000 WU (txmempool.cpp:179-181). The division by four happens only at the consumer boundary, ToFeePerVSize (policy/policy.h:196). So we apply the per-transaction ceiling BEFORE the cross-multiplied comparisons in %feefrac-cross (src/mempool/feefrac.lisp:46-51) instead of after: two transactions whose weights differ by 1..3 WU become indistinguishable, and per-transaction rounding accumulates against the cluster cap.
consequence: Three distinct effects, all bounded by the sub-1% rounding, all executed against the CURRENT txgraph (the incremental chunk index just landed on main). (1) Chunk BOUNDARIES differ, not merely tie order: a CPFP pair whose child has strictly higher feerate in weight units has equal feerate in our vbytes, so Core forms one chunk and we form two. That changes eviction -- txgraph-get-worst-main-chunk hands the trimmer the child alone where Core evicts the parent-and-child pair -- and therefore the set of transactions dropped and the rolling minimum fee bump computed from the evicted chunk. (2) Mining order can strictly FLIP, not just fall back to a tie-break: two singleton clusters ordered X-then-Y by Core's fee-per-weight are ordered Y-then-X by our fee-per-vbyte. (3) The cluster size limit is strictly stricter than Core's: because each transaction's vsize is rounded up individually, a 64-transaction cluster of total weight 403812 WU (well inside Core's 404000) sums to 101001 vB and we report the graph oversized, rejecting an admission Core accepts as :too-large-cluster. The window is at most 3 WU per transaction, so at 64 transactions the cap is up to 48 vB (192 WU) tighter. None of this makes an invalid block or an invalid relay decision, so S3, not S2 -- but the docstrings understate it: src/mining/assembler.lisp:258-266 claims chunk feerates order 'matching Core's fee/adjusted-weight ordering up to the per-tx ceiling' and src/mempool/mempool.lisp:52-58 claims the cluster limit 'matches up to the per-tx ceiling', and the chunk-boundary, strict-flip and cap cases show the qualifier is doing more work than it looks. src/rpc/mempool.lisp:289-292 is also wrong on its face: it says our txgraph measures BIP141 virtual bytes, when it measures SIGOP-ADJUSTED virtual bytes.

fix_shape: Move the division to the consumer boundary, as Core does. Add a sigop-adjusted WEIGHT accessor (max(weight, sigops * bytes-per-sigop), no ceiling) alongside sigop-adjusted-vsize, feed THAT to txgraph-add-transaction at src/mempool/mempool.lisp:1008-1010 and :1404, and set +max-cluster-size+ to 404000 (Core's cluster_size_vbytes * WITNESS_SCALE_FACTOR) with *cluster-size-limit* scaled the same way, keeping the 101 kvB knob as the configured value so the -limitclustersize contract is unchanged.
